results.title: Kris Aquino’s visit to First Lady, a sign of ‘good ties’ — Palace
results.description: Malacañang described the recent visit of Kris Aquino and her sons, Josh and Bimby, to First Lady Liza Areneta-Marcos as a sign of good ties between their families. Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro said that although the First Lady has not yet shared anything about the visit, it already suggests that "they have a good relationship." "Actually, I tried to ask the First Lady about that. Wala pa siya ni-share sa akin. Pero nakita naman natin kung ano iyong pahiwatig ng pagbisita ni Kris, ni Ms. Kris Aquino at ng kaniyang mga anak, nagpapahiwatig ito na maganda ang kanilang relasyon (Actually, I tried to ask the First Lady about that. She hasn’t shared anything with me yet. But we saw what the visit of Ms. Kris Aquino and her children seems to indicate. It suggests that they have a good relationship)," Castro said in a Palace briefing on Tuesday, Aug.11. As for what they discussed, nothing has been shared yet; they were definitely happy with the visit, Castro added. "Kung ano iyong kanilang pag-usapan, wala po naibibigay sa akin at kung mayroon man ay baka hindi pa ako allowed sabihin ito (As for what they discussed, nothing has been shared with me. And if there is something, perhaps I’m not yet allowed to disclose it)," the Palace spokesperson said. "But definitely masaya naman sila, pero kapag naibigay sa atin ni First Lady, ang mga magaganda nilang naging usapan, ishi-share ko naman iyan sa inyo (But definitely, they’re happy. If the First Lady shares with us the good things they talked about, I’ll definitely share them with you)," she added. The First Lady shared about the Aquinos' visit in a Facebook post on Sunday, Aug. 9. They brought several cakes for the First Lady ahead of her Aug. 21 birthday. She thanked them for the surprise, saying it was "such a thoughtful surprise that truly warmed my heart."

results.title: True crime is having a moment, and Stephanie Soo is taking it to Netflix
results.description: True crime has become a familiar part of the local podcast and streaming landscape, with Filipino audiences tuning in to stories about real-life crimes, mysteries and cases that continue to spark discussion. That audience includes fans of Stephanie Soo, whose "Rotten Mango" podcast has built a strong following around these parts. Note the show currently sits at No. 4 on Apple Podcasts' overall chart for the country. Now, Soo is taking her brand of true crime storytelling to Netflix. The creator behind "Rotten Mango" is set to headline "The Rotten Files with Stephanie Soo," a new Netflix original true-crime podcast that will have her looking into some of the most talked-about and disturbing cases making headlines. The project gives Soo a new platform after years of building an audience online. The appeal of "Rotten Mango" has largely been Soo's willingness to spend time on the details of a case. Her episodes often go beyond simply recounting what happened, digging into the people involved, the circumstances surrounding the crime and the psychology behind it. "The Rotten Files" brings her back to the genre that made "Rotten Mango" a hit. "Netflix is putting meaningful creative power in the hands of content creators, which is a really rare opportunity," Soo said. "We’re ready to hit the ground running." "The Rotten Files with Stephanie Soo" is scheduled to premiere on Netflix on Aug. 14.
